problems.comment:
As a consequence of new snow and a strong to storm force westerly wind, sometimes avalanche prone wind slabs will form. The new snow and wind slabs are lying on top of a weakly bonded old snowpack in particular on steep shady slopes above approximately 2600 m. 
 Avalanches can be released by a single winter sport participant. Mostly they are medium-sized. 
 Backcountry touring calls for experience in the assessment of avalanche danger.

bulletin.snowpack:
The snow depths are average for the time of year. Above approximately 2800 m there is 50 to 80 cm of snow. New and wind-drifted snow is being deposited on an old snowpack that contains weak layers on high-altitude shady slopes. In some places avalanches can also be triggered in these deeper layers.
Below approximately 2600 m, the snow depths are still relatively low, so that despite rain only small and medium-sized wet avalanches are to be expected.
bulletin.tendency: The danger of dry avalanches will increase. Even single winter sport participants can release avalanches in many places. These can also be triggered in deeper layers and reach dangerously large size. Natural avalanches are possible. The conditions are critical for backcountry touring and other off-piste activities.

problems.comment:
As a consequence of new snow and a strong to storm force westerly wind, avalanche prone wind slabs will form. The new snow and wind slabs are lying on top of a weakly bonded old snowpack in particular on steep shady slopes above approximately 2600 m. 
 The number and size of avalanche prone locations will increase as the day progresses. An increasing number of natural avalanches are possible. Avalanches can be released by a single winter sport participant and reach large size in isolated cases. 
 Backcountry touring calls for experience in the assessment of avalanche danger and careful route selection.
